{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D25", "D33", "D42"],
      "pins": ["D25.2", "D33.2", "D42.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0193"],
      "observed": "The common anode net /NET0193 connects only to the anode pins of D25, D33 and D42. No supply or driver reaches it. Each LED's cathode is driven through a series resistor from a CM4 status line (R101 from Module2 pin 15 nLED3, R14 from Module2 pin 17 nLED2, R30 from NET0142 / Module2 pin 21 PI_nLED_Activity).",
      "expected": "A common-anode LED bank should have its anode tied to +3V3 (as D4, D17 and D21 are). Otherwise the status LEDs cannot be driven by the active-low cathode signals.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"46\") (name \"/NET0193\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D25\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D33\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D42\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"102\") (name \"NET0122\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"Module2\") (pin \"17\") (pinfunction \"Ethernet_nLED2(3.3v)\") (pintype \"output\")) (node (ref \"R14\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\")))"}
      ],
      "impact": "Three status LEDs (Ethernet/PI activity indicators) never light, because their anode bank is not connected to a supply.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["U22", "Q9"],
      "pins": ["U22.1", "U22.6", "Q9.2", "Q9.3"],
      "nets": ["/NET0031", "+5V"],
      "observed": "The LTC4412 VIN pin and the USB-C VBUS nets (NET0031, which includes J27 A4/A9/B4/B9) share a node with the Q9 drain. The SENSE pin and Q9 source sit on +5V, the buck output. The PMOS is oriented with its source on the regulated side and its drain on VBUS.",
      "expected": "In the ideal-diode OR-ing arrangement the PMOS source should be on the input supply (VBUS). Its drain should feed the common +5V load, with SENSE on the load side. This keeps the body diode blocking reverse current from +5V back to USB, which is the stated purpose of U6/Q9.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"62\") (name \"NET0031\") ... (node (ref \"Q9\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") (pintype \"passive\")) ... (node (ref \"U22\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"VIN\") (pintype \"power_in\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+5V\") ... (node (ref \"Q9\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") (pintype \"passive\")) ... (node (ref \"U22\") (pin \"6\") (pinfunction \"SENSE\") (pintype \"input\")))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, `U6`)"}
      ],
      "impact": "The PMOS body diode can conduct from the 5 V rail back into the USB VBUS line. The reverse-current protection the design depends on is defeated, and the ideal-diode path may not behave as intended.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R84", "R35", "L3", "U5"],
      "pins": ["R84.1", "R84.2", "R35.1", "R35.2", "U5.3"],
      "nets": ["/NET0196", "+12V"],
      "observed": "The boost regulator U5 (TPS61040) FB node NET0196 is set by R84 = 1.8M to +12V and R35 = 205k to GND. That ratio gives an output of roughly 2 V for a ~0.2 V reference, not the 12 V that the +12V net is supposed to carry.",
      "expected": "The feedback divider for a 12 V output from a ~0.2 V reference needs a top/bottom ratio near 59:1. With R84 = 1.8M, R35 should be about 30 kΩ, not 205 kΩ.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"131\") (name \"NET0196\") ... (node (ref \"R84\") (pin \"1\") ...) (node (ref \"R35\") (pin \"2\") ...) (node (ref \"U5\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"FB\") ...))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R35 0 NET0196 205k"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R84 NET0196 +12V 1.8Meg"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the value is wrong, the 12 V boost rail would regulate far below its intended voltage, which affects the devices powered from +12V.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The most likely anomaly is the status-LED anode bank (D25, D33, D42) whose common anode net connects to nothing, leaving those LEDs unable to light. Lower-confidence concerns are the LTC4412 PMOS orientation and the boost feedback divider value."
}

anomalies.observed: The common anode net /NET0193 connects only to the anode pins of D25, D33 and D42. No supply or driver reaches it. Each LED's cathode is driven through a series resistor from a CM4 status line (R101 from Module2 pin 15 nLED3, R14 from Module2 pin 17 nLED2, R30 from NET0142 / Module2 pin 21 PI_nLED_Activity).
anomalies.expected: A common-anode LED bank should have its anode tied to +3V3 (as D4, D17 and D21 are). Otherwise the status LEDs cannot be driven by the active-low cathode signals.
anomalies.impact: Three status LEDs (Ethernet/PI activity indicators) never light, because their anode bank is not connected to a supply.

anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 VIN pin and the USB-C VBUS nets (NET0031, which includes J27 A4/A9/B4/B9) share a node with the Q9 drain. The SENSE pin and Q9 source sit on +5V, the buck output. The PMOS is oriented with its source on the regulated side and its drain on VBUS.
anomalies.expected: In the ideal-diode OR-ing arrangement the PMOS source should be on the input supply (VBUS). Its drain should feed the common +5V load, with SENSE on the load side. This keeps the body diode blocking reverse current from +5V back to USB, which is the stated purpose of U6/Q9.
anomalies.impact: The PMOS body diode can conduct from the 5 V rail back into the USB VBUS line. The reverse-current protection the design depends on is defeated, and the ideal-diode path may not behave as intended.

anomalies.observed: The boost regulator U5 (TPS61040) FB node NET0196 is set by R84 = 1.8M to +12V and R35 = 205k to GND. That ratio gives an output of roughly 2 V for a ~0.2 V reference, not the 12 V that the +12V net is supposed to carry.
anomalies.expected: The feedback divider for a 12 V output from a ~0.2 V reference needs a top/bottom ratio near 59:1. With R84 = 1.8M, R35 should be about 30 kΩ, not 205 kΩ.
anomalies.impact: If the value is wrong, the 12 V boost rail would regulate far below its intended voltage, which affects the devices powered from +12V.
